correctness.rationale: Rooted-forest decomposition bijectively counts connected simple unicyclic graphs. Deleting specified noncycle leaves gives every joint event exactly; factorial moments and inclusion-exclusion yield conditional occupancy. Strict regression follows from an explicit positive first difference. Truncated-Poisson cycle representation and conditional Poissonization plus a full-lattice local CLT prove independent leading fluctuations. Exact asymptotic regression expansion and moment convergence yield the nonzero covariance constant. The standalone verifier exhausts all connected unicyclic graphs through seven vertices and reports 86 exact aggregate identities, supporting but not replacing the general proof.

originality.rationale: The conditional multivariate leaf-empty-box law and its cycle-regression/second-order mixed covariance were compared by implication with known rooted-forest enumeration, unicyclic generating functions, degree-statistic asymptotics, and related published results. Classical precursor facts are excluded from the novelty claim. Nothing read states or immediately implies the entire paired theorem without the distinct deletion/occupancy and conditional-normal steps; residual implicit-generating-function coverage remains a nontrivial risk.

value.rationale: An exact conditional law for the whole degree-one vertex count at each cycle length, and its sharp finite-size conditional-mean regression, are natural statistics of single-cycle random graph components. The order-sqrt(n) covariance constant alongside asymptotically independent half-normal and Gaussian leading limits exposes a dependence scale invisible to separate marginal CLTs. The result has motivated, independently applicable mathematical content rather than a parameter-relabeling or an arbitrary finite cutoff.
